newsitem.title: ITALY: FOCUS-Benetton issues shares to up dividend.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Benetton issues shares to up dividend.

text.p: Italian clothing giant Benetton announced a free issue of shares to investors on Friday to help boost overall dividend payouts.
It also said it would issue bonds of up to 500 billion lire ($294.4 million).

Many analysts saw the free share issue as a method of increasing the aggregate dividend payout to Benetton's shareholders as the clothing manufacturer is set to move into a net cash position as it eliminates net debt.

Benetton said it proposes to pay a stock dividend via the issue of one bonus share for every 25 held with dividend rights from January 1, 1997, and to issue bonds totalling up to 500 billion lire on the domestic and international markets.

For Silvia Roveda of Italian brokers Centrosim the free share issue was a positive sign as the issue should have no effect on the actual dividend payment per share planned for 1996. She and some other analysts already forecast a rise in the 1996 dividend to 450 lire from 425 lire a share.
With Benetton's 1996 results due at the end of March, Roveda was keeping her share recommendation for Benetton as a hold.

Other analysts said the extra four percent of shares in issue would effectively boost the dividend payout by the company by the same amount. One analyst looking for a dividend of 475 lire a share said the extra four percent would push the effective dividend payment to investors up to near 500 lire.

Andrea Beghetti at brokers Eptasim said the extra shares would help to increase the liquidity of the shares in the market, and he is targetting a level of 24,000 lire by the year-end. Benetton Group SpA is 71.3 percent owned by the Benetton family company Edizioni Holding.
Benetton said the stock dividend, "reflecting positive results achieved thus far and the healthy outlook for the future" will be more than covered out of available reserves.

The allocation of these bonus shares will be additional to the payment of a fair cash dividend, to be proposed to stockholders by the board when it meets to formally approve 1996 financial statements, a company statement said.
Analysts said the bond issues were likely to be aimed at refinancing rolling debts at advantageous rates.
"The bond issue will reshape the profile of current borrowing, by diversifying sources of finance to include more frequent recourse to the capital markets," it added.
Benetton shares ended up 0.46 percent at 20,800 lire in a firmer Milan stock market. ($ = 1698 Italian Lire)
